label: History
value: Mr. Allan brought his young bride to Avonlea five years before the current time.
unit: Having brought his young bride to Avonlea five years prior, Mr. Allan served as the town's minister. During a social visit to Green Gables early in his tenure, he and his wife attended a tea prepared by Anne, where Mrs. Allan accidentally sampled a layer cake flavored with anodyne liniment. Following the sudden death of Matthew Cuthbert, Mr. Allan provided spiritual support and comfort to Anne as she grieved. His eventual departure from Avonlea was noted by the local community as Anne completed her tenure as the town's schoolteacher.

label: History
value: Anne Shirley grew up as a fourteen-year-old orphan
unit: Anne Shirley grew up as a fourteen-year-old orphan with no known family before being adopted by Marilla and Matthew Cuthbert at Green Gables. Though sent by mistake instead of a boy, she was permitted to stay and settled into Avonlea, where she accidentally got her best friend Diana Barry drunk on currant wine, accidentally dyed her red hair green with peddler's dye, fell off a roof during a dare, and accidentally seasoned a cake with liniment. After studying at Queen's Academy and passing her exams, she gave up a college scholarship to stay at Green Gables and teach locally when Marilla's eyesight began to fail, reconciling with her rival Gilbert Blythe when he gave up the Avonlea school so she could have it. As an Avonlea teacher, Anne accidentally sold her neighbor's cow, accidentally applied rug dye to her nose before hosting important guests, and rejected an unromantic marriage proposal sent on behalf of Billy Andrews. Moving on to Redmond College with Priscilla Grant, she formed a close friendship with Philippa Gordon and moved into Patty's Place with her friends and Aunt Jamesina. Along the way, Diana submitted one of Anne's stories to a baking powder contest without her permission, leading to a dismayed Anne winning first prize with commercial edits added to her work. Over the course of her college years, Anne refused a romantic marriage proposal from Gilbert Blythe, spent time teaching at Valley Road, and successfully published a short sketch. At the end of her college life, Anne rejected a proposal from her wealthy suitor, Roy Gardner, after realizing in the moment that she did not love him.

unit: Anne Shirley grew up as a fourteen-year-old orphan with no known family before being adopted by Marilla and Matthew Cuthbert at Green Gables. Though sent by mistake instead of a boy, she was permitted to stay and settled into Avonlea, where she accidentally got her best friend Diana Barry drunk on currant wine, accidentally dyed her red hair green with peddler's dye, fell off a roof during a dare, and accidentally seasoned a cake with liniment. After studying at Queen's Academy and passing her exams, she gave up a college scholarship to stay at Green Gables and teach locally when Marilla's eyesight began to fail, reconciling with her rival Gilbert Blythe when he gave up the Avonlea school so she could have it. As an Avonlea teacher, Anne accidentally sold her neighbor's cow, accidentally applied rug dye to her nose before hosting important guests, and rejected an unromantic marriage proposal sent on behalf of Billy Andrews. Moving on to Redmond College with Priscilla Grant, she formed a close friendship with Philippa Gordon and moved into Patty's Place with her friends and Aunt Jamesina. Along the way, Diana submitted one of Anne's stories to a baking powder contest without her permission, leading to a dismayed Anne winning first prize with commercial edits added to her work. Over the course of her college years, Anne refused a romantic marriage proposal from Gilbert Blythe, spent time teaching at Valley Road, and successfully published a short sketch. At the end of her college life, Anne rejected a proposal from her wealthy suitor, Roy Gardner, after realizing in the moment that she did not love him.

Though sent by mistake instead of a boy, she was permitted to stay and settled into Avonlea, where she accidentally got her best friend Diana Barry drunk on currant wine, accidentally dyed her red hair green with peddler's dye, fell off a roof during a dare, and accidentally seasoned a cake with liniment. After studying at Queen's Academy and passing her exams, she gave up a college scholarship to stay at Green Gables and teach locally when Marilla's eyesight began to fail, reconciling with her rival Gilbert Blythe when he gave up the Avonlea school so she could have it. As an Avonlea teacher, Anne accidentally sold her neighbor's cow, accidentally applied rug dye to her nose before hosting important guests, and rejected an unromantic marriage proposal sent on behalf of Billy Andrews. Moving on to Redmond College with Priscilla Grant, she formed a close friendship with Philippa Gordon and moved into Patty's Place with her friends and Aunt Jamesina. Along the way, Diana submitted one of Anne's stories to a baking powder contest without her permission, leading to a dismayed Anne winning first prize with commercial edits added to her work. Over the course of her college years, Anne refused a romantic marriage proposal from Gilbert Blythe, spent time teaching at Valley Road, and successfully published a short sketch. At the end of her college life, Anne rejected a proposal from her wealthy suitor, Roy Gardner, after realizing in the moment that she did not love him.

label: Quote
value: Anne Shirley said: "I’ll fold them nicely tonight. They always made us do that at the asylum. Half the time, though, I’d forget, I’d be in such a hurry to get into bed nice and quiet and imagine things."

label: Quote
value: Anne Shirley said: "I’d do anything to oblige you. But you’ll have to tell me what to say for this once. After I get into bed I’ll imagine out a real nice prayer to say always. I believe that it will be quite interesting, now that I come to think of it."

label: Quote
value: Anne Shirley said: "But I’d be ever so much gratefuller if—if you’d made just one of them with puffed sleeves. Puffed sleeves are so fashionable now. It would give me such a thrill, Marilla, just to wear a dress with puffed sleeves."

label: Quote
value: Anne Shirley said: "Oh, Marilla, I’m frightened—now that it has come I’m actually frightened. What if she shouldn’t like me! It would be the most tragical disappointment of my life."

label: Quote
value: Anne Shirley said: "I’ll just eat one tonight, Marilla. And I can give Diana half of them, can’t I? The other half will taste twice as sweet to me if I give some to her. It’s delightful to think I have something to give her."

label: History
value: Anne was orphaned as an infant.
unit: Orphaned as an infant and raised outside Prince Edward Island during a lonely, starved childhood, Anne was adopted out of an orphan asylum by Marilla and Matthew Cuthbert to live at Green Gables. Though initially met with skepticism due to her intense imagination and fierce temper, Anne quickly proved her worth by apologizing for a outburst against Mrs. Rachel Lynde, helping around the farm, and saving the life of Diana Barry's baby sister. She excelled academically, forming an intense rivalry with Gilbert Blythe, starting a story club, and eventually tying for first place on the Island's Queen's Academy entrance examinations. After earning the Avery scholarship at Queen's and enduring the devastating death of her beloved Matthew from a sudden heart attack, Anne chose to stay at Green Gables to support Marilla. While working as a local schoolteacher and helping found the Village Improvement Society, she inadvertently took in the mischievous orphaned twins Davy and Dora Keith. Anne later pursued higher education at Redmond College, securing her financial future thanks to a thousand-dollar bequest from the late Miss Josephine Barry and finally reading a collection of her deceased parents' love letters in her birthplace of Bolingbroke. Throughout her young adulthood, Anne navigated several clumsy marriage proposals—including ones from Jane Andrews on behalf of her brother Billy, Sam, and her long-time suitor Royal Gardner—while mistakenly believing Gilbert Blythe was engaged to someone else. Upon learning that Gilbert was near death from typhoid fever, Anne finally recognized her deep romantic feelings for him. Following his miraculous recovery, Anne accepted Gilbert's proposal in Hester Gray's garden, happily agreeing to marry him.

value: Aunt Jamesina is a sweet woman.
unit: Aunt Jamesina is a sweet, old-fashioned woman who admits that both her clothes and opinions reflect her traditional ways. Though she holds a low opinion of Phil, she compensates by loving her deeply.

label: History
value: Aunt Jamesina never attended college.
unit: Though she never attended college herself, Aunt Jamesina moved into Patty's Place to act as housekeeper for her niece Stella Maynard, Anne Shirley, Priscilla, and Phil Gordon. She brought along her two cats, Joseph and the Sarah-cat, and quickly established a warm, relaxed household routine with the girls. Over their years together, Aunt Jamesina regularly shared conversation, advice, and stories of her own youth and past suitors with the household as the young women navigated their studies and romances. She remained a comforting presence at Patty's Place through their graduations up until the friends packed up the house at the end of their college life.

value: Aunt Jamesina said: "She couldn’t take Joseph with her so she begged me to take him. I really couldn’t refuse. He’s a beautiful cat—that is, his disposition is beautiful. She called him Joseph because his coat is of many colors."

label: Quote
value: Aunt Jamesina said: "Kittens have to be drowned, I admit, or the world would be overrun. But no decent, grown-up cat should be done to death—unless he sucks eggs."

label: Quote
value: Aunt Jamesina said: "Well, I hope so, Anne. I do hope so, because I love her. But I can’t understand her—she beats me. She isn’t like any of the girls I ever knew, or any of the girls I was myself."

label: Quote
value: Aunt Jamesina said: "Yes, in my soul. But I’ll admit my legs aren’t as young as yours. You go and get some fresh air, Anne. You look pale lately."

label: Quote
value: Aunt Jamesina said: "Anybody is liable to rheumatism in her legs, Anne. It’s only old people who should have rheumatism in their souls, though. Thank goodness, I never have. When you get rheumatism in your soul you might as well go and pick out your coffin."

label: History
value: Aunt Josephine is the great-aunt of Diana Barry.
unit: Aunt Josephine was the wealthy great-aunt of Diana Barry who lived at Beechwood in Charlottetown. During a visit to Orchard Slope, she was infuriated when Anne Shirley and Diana accidentally jumped on top of her in the spare-room bed, but she was so won over by Anne's brave, sincere apology that she decided to stay in Avonlea and became firm friends with her. She later sent Anne kid slippers for Christmas and hosted Anne and Diana at her estate for the Exhibition in Charlottetown. After enduring a dreadful illness that lasted over a year, Aunt Josephine passed away, leaving Anne a legacy of one thousand dollars in her will to secure her college education.

label: History
value: Charlotta the Fourth was a fourteen-year-old girl.
unit: Charlotta the Fourth was a fourteen-year-old girl who lived at Echo Lodge as a maid for Miss Lavendar Lewis. She often hosted visiting guests alongside her employer, serving tea, picking strawberries, and sharing her anxieties about Miss Lavendar's melancholy behavior. When Stephen Irving returned to rekindle his romance with Miss Lavendar, Charlotta helped Anne prepare for his arrival and anxiously awaited the outcome in the kitchen until she witnessed their joyful reconciliation. She subsequently assisted in the hectic preparations for Miss Lavendar and Stephen's garden wedding at Echo Lodge.

label: Quote
value: Charlotta said: "it’s plain to be seen you and Miss Lavendar have got a secret and I think, begging your pardon if I’m too forward, Miss Shirley, ma’am, that it’s real mean not to tell me when we’ve all been such chums."

label: Quote
value: Charlotta said: "I peeked from the kitchen window . . . and he’s awful handsome . . . and just the right age for Miss Lavendar. And oh, Miss Shirley, ma’am, do you think it would be much harm to listen at the door?"

label: Quote
value: Charlotta said: "But I’m sure I shan’t sleep a blessed wink, Miss Shirley, ma’am, for fear that something’ll go wrong at the last minute . . . the cream won’t whip . . . or Mr. Irving’ll have a stroke and not be able to come."

label: Quote
value: Charlotta said: "but there’s so much to do yet . . . and oh, Miss Shirley, ma’am, I’m skeered it’s going to rain and I wish you’d get up and tell me you think it ain’t."

label: Quote
value: Charlotta said: "Yes, ma’am. Come in, ma’am. I’ll tell Miss Lavendar you’re here, ma’am. She’s upstairs, ma’am."

label: History
value: Davy Keith was born an orphan.
unit: Davy Keith was born an orphan after losing his father as a baby and going without cake for a long time during his mother's illness. Following a long conversation with his mother the night before she died, Davy and his twin sister, Dora, were taken in for the winter by Marilla Cuthbert to live at Green Gables. Unaccustomed to proper bringing up, Davy quickly gained a reputation for wild antics, such as dropping a caterpillar down a church attendee's neck, forcing Dora to walk a pigpen fence, and hiding a toad in Marilla's bed. He also locked Dora inside Mr. Harrison's toolhouse, though he broke down in tears over his falsehoods when confronted by Anne Shirley. Despite his misbehavior, including eating lemon pies intended for a famous visiting author and struggling with bedtime prayers, Anne consistently guided him with patience. The twins' stay at Green Gables became permanent after their relative Richard Keith died and left them a trust fund. As he grew older, Davy continued to act out by cutting up Dora's aprons, scaring Mrs. Rachel Lynde with a jack-o'-lantern, and chasing her rooster until it died. On one occasion, he convinced Dora to skip Sunday School to go fishing with the Cottons and lied to Mrs. Lynde, but his guilty conscience eventually drove him to confess to Anne late at night so she could encourage him to seek forgiveness. Over the years, Davy remained an enthusiastic presence at Green Gables, eagerly welcoming Anne home from Redmond College during her visits, chattering about his lost tooth, complaining about his arithmetic schoolwork, and looking forward to future marriage plans.

label: History
value: Diana was named at birth by a schoolmaster who was boarding at her home.
unit: Named at birth by a schoolmaster who was boarding at her home, Diana grew up alongside Anne, with whom she swore an oath of friendship, helped establish a schoolgirl story club, named local landmarks like Lover's Lane, and imagined ghosts in the Haunted Wood. She took a trip to Carmody where her aunt taught her a fancy new crochet stitch. When Anne accidentally served her currant wine instead of raspberry cordial, Diana became dizzy and ill, leading her mother to forbid them from playing together until Anne later saved Diana's sister Minnie May from croup. Diana later received a pair of kid slippers from her Aunt Josephine, which she gave to Anne on Christmas morning before they both performed in a school concert. She accompanied Anne to Charlottetown for the Exhibition, staying at her Aunt Josephine's Beechwood estate, and later rushed to Green Gables to break the news that Anne had tied for first place on the Island on the Queen's Entrance exams. After walking down the aisle to marry Fred Wright at Orchard Slope, Diana gave birth to a baby boy, whom Anne visited upon returning home from college.

value: Diana said: “Those Pye girls are cheats all round,” said Diana indignantly, as they climbed the fence of the main road. “Gertie Pye actually went and put her milk bottle in my place in the brook yesterday. Did you ever? I don’t speak to her now.”

label: Quote
value: Diana said: "Why, he makes fun of all the girls. He laughs at mine because it’s so black. He’s called me a crow a dozen times; and I never heard him apologize for anything before, either."

label: Quote
value: Diana said: "I do think you’re mean. What shall I do? Mr. Phillips will make me sit with that horrid Gertie Pye—I know he will because she is sitting alone. Do come back, Anne."

unit: Aunt Josephine is Diana's great-aunt, an elder relation whom Diana visits in Charlottetown. Their relationship ran into severe drama when Diana and Anne accidentally leaped onto her in a spare-room bed during a game, leaving the old lady furious and threatening Diana's music lessons. The situation was mended when Anne personally apologized, and Aunt Josephine later showed warmth toward the girls, including inviting Diana and Anne to stay at her estate for the Charlottetown Exhibition.

label: Personality
value: Dora is a young girl.
unit: Dora is a remarkably quiet, demure, and well-behaved young girl who is considered a model child. Known for her neatness, industry, and faithful nature, she carries out her small duties carefully and systematically, never needing to be told how to do a task twice. She maintains a prim, proper, and placid demeanor, remaining composed and composedly silent unless spoken to directly. Though her steady, dispassionate approach to life makes her reliable, others note her somewhat monotonous temperament and note that her prim nature makes her less suited as a playmate for rowdy games. Despite her usual composure, she harbors a specific fear regarding Mirabel Cotton's deceased uncle.

label: History
value: Gilbert Blythe returned to Avonlea
unit: Gilbert Blythe returned to Avonlea after three years in Alberta, where he had hardly attended school while caring for his sick father, and immediately resumed his studies alongside Anne Shirley. Their initial meeting resulted in Anne breaking a slate over his head after he teased her, sparking a fierce academic rivalry. During a dory accident on the pond, Gilbert rescued Anne and offered an apology, but she refused his friendship. The two later tied for first place on the Island for the Queen's Entrance examinations and went on to attend Queen's Academy together, where Gilbert won the academic medal. Upon graduating, Gilbert gave up his secured teaching position in Avonlea so that Anne could remain close to Green Gables, prompting a reconciliation between them. Together, they established the Village Improvement Society and maintained a close friendship while preparing for Redmond College. During their freshman year at Redmond, Gilbert gained distinction by leading the Freshmen to victory in the Arts Rush and served as captain of the football team. His feelings for Anne deepened, but when he proposed to her in the garden at Patty's Place, she rejected him, insisting she only cared for him as a friend. Following the rejection, Gilbert began spending time with Christine Stuart, and he went on to win High Honors in Classics and the Cooper Prize upon completing his degree. Shortly after graduation, Gilbert suffered a severe case of typhoid fever back in Avonlea, but his fever broke and he recovered. Once restored to health, he asked Anne to walk with him to Hester Gray's garden, where he proposed a second time, and she accepted.

value: Harrison is a crusty old man.

He is a pipe-smoker, a regular churchgoer who subscribes to the salary, and harbors a clear prejudice against marriage. Despising being pitied, he strategically wears a white collar during business transactions so that he appears prosperous enough to prevent others from trying to cheat him.

label: History
value: Harrison was an old bachelor
unit: Before moving to Avonlea, Harrison was an old bachelor who lived in Scottsford, New Brunswick, having delayed getting married for a long time. His initial encounter with Anne Shirley was a heated argument after her cow strayed into his oats, but their relationship quickly mended when Anne accidentally sold his Jersey cow and came to offer a replacement and a baked cake. label: Quote
value: Harrison said: “Who? Mrs. Lynde? Don’t you tell me I’m like that old gossip,” said Mr. Harrison irritably. “I’m not . . . not a bit. What have you got in that box?”

label: Quote
value: Harrison said: "I don’t, that’s a fact, and I’m mighty fond of it, too. I’m much obliged to you. It looks good on top. I hope it’s good all the way through."

label: Quote
value: Harrison said: "Well, I’ll tell you what, miss, you must help me eat it. I’ll put the kettle on and we’ll have a cup of tea. How will that do?"

label: Quote
value: Harrison said: "I see you haven’t much confidence in my ability to make tea. You’re wrong . . . I can brew up as good a jorum of tea as you ever drank. But go ahead yourself. Fortunately it rained last Sunday, so there’s plenty of clean dishes."

label: Quote
value: Harrison said: “I’m a crusty, lonesome, crabbed old chap,” he said aloud, “but there’s something about that little girl makes me feel young again . . . and it’s such a pleasant sensation I’d like to have it repeated once in a while.”

unit: During her schooldays in Avonlea, Jane Andrews was a member of the local "Story Club" alongside Anne Shirley and other classmates. As a young adult, she attended a summer concert at the White Sands Hotel with Anne and Diana, riding home with her brother Billy after the event. Years later, Jane met with Anne and proposed to her on behalf of Billy; after Anne declined the offer, Jane coolly accepted the refusal, noting that her brother would likely marry Nettie Blewett instead.

label: Personality
value: Jane is a plain individual.
unit: Jane is a plain, practical, and conscientious individual known for her steady, sensible, and lady-like demeanor. While recognized as nice and dutiful, she can also be strict and is noted for being crosser than Anne, particularly when dealing with pupils who make funny speeches. Initially, her goal was to devote her entire life to teaching, remain unmarried, earn her salary fairly, please the school trustees, and earn a spot on the School Inspector's roll of honor. However, she eventually marries, though her exceptional cooking skills present a unique challenge when her husband refuses to let her cook.

label: History
value: Jane Andrews grew up in Avonlea
unit: Jane Andrews grew up in Avonlea as a friend and schoolmate of Anne Shirley. During their school years, she joined Anne's newly formed story club and entered the preparation class for Queen's Academy. After passing the entrance examination alongside her classmates, she attended Queen's Academy and later took up a position teaching at the local Avonlea school. Jane formed a close bond with Anne and her peers, participating in a spring birthday outing through the woods and joining a committee for the Village Improvement Society that successfully convinced Judson Parker not to place advertisements on his fence. Later, Jane resigned from teaching in Avonlea with plans to move West in the fall. Before her planned departure, Jane hosted Anne for an overnight stay and proposed to her on behalf of her shy brother, Billy. Though Anne turned down the offer, Jane accepted the refusal composedly, remarking that Billy would likely marry someone else instead.

label: History
value: Miss Janet Sweet was a resident of Valley Road.
unit: Miss Janet Sweet was a resident of Valley Road who lived at Wayside, where she took in Anne Shirley as a boarder during Anne's time as a local schoolteacher. For twenty years, Janet was courted by her neighbor John Douglas, though he never proposed; on her fortieth birthday, she broke down in tears over the situation and briefly snubbed John following Anne's advice to stand up for herself. After John's overbearing mother passed away, John revealed that a secret oath to his late mother had prevented him from marrying, and he finally proposed to Janet.

label: Quote
value: Janet said: "Oh, she does. She’s told me time and again that she’d love to see John settled before her time comes. She’s always giving him hints—you heard her yourself the other day. I thought I’d ha’ gone through the floor."

label: Quote
value: Janet said: "You see, Anne, I’ve always been awful fond of John. He might just as well keep coming as not, for there was never anybody else I’d want, so it didn’t matter."

label: Quote
value: Janet said: "No, I guess not. I was afraid to try, anyway, for fear he’d think I meant it and just go. I suppose I’m a poor-spirited creature, but that is how I feel. And I can’t help it."

label: Quote
value: Janet said: "I know the road home pretty well alone. I ought to, seeing I’ve been traveling it for forty years. So you needn’t trouble yourself, Mr. Douglas."

label: Quote
value: Janet said: "Oh, I’m just as glad you did. When I saw John Douglas making off down that road I just felt as if every little bit of joy and happiness that was left in my life was going with him. It was an awful feeling."

Shortly after his mother passed away, John visited Wayside and proposed to Janet, revealing that his late mother had forced him to swear a secret oath never to marry while she was still alive.

Though she initially found him funny and ugly, Jonas delivered a deeply moving sermon that earned her profound admiration and left her contemplating whether she was falling in love with him.

label: History
value: Joseph is a cat.
unit: Joseph is a cat with a multicolored coat who originally belonged to a dear friend of Aunt Jamesina before being given to her when his owner moved to Vancouver. He was brought to Patty's Place alongside Aunt Jamesina and the Sarah-cat. After engaging in repeated battles with Rusty, a stray cat adopted by Anne, Joseph eventually became Rusty's close friend. He later contributed to the household chaos at Patty's Place during an unexpected visit from Roy Gardner's mother and sisters.

label: History
value: Josie Pye was the last of her family to attend the Avonlea school.
unit: Josie Pye was the last of her family to attend the Avonlea school, where she had once earned first prize for knitted lace at the exhibition. During a party at Diana Barry's house, she challenged Anne Shirley to walk the ridgepole of Mr. Barry's roof, an act that resulted in Anne falling and breaking her ankle. Later, Josie was among the group of Avonlea students who attended the local school under Miss Stacy's guidance and eventually pursued higher education at Queen's Academy.

label: History
value: Lavendar Lewis lived at Echo Lodge.
unit: Lavendar Lewis lived at Echo Lodge with her young maid, Charlotta the Fourth, named by her father after lavender because he loved its scent. After getting lost on a walk, Anne Shirley and Diana Barry met Miss Lavendar, and a quiet sadness came over her when Anne accidentally mentioned Paul Irving. Miss Lavendar later opened up to Anne about her past romance and broken engagement with Paul's father, Stephen Irving, prompting Anne to introduce young Paul to her, and the two quickly formed a warm connection. After Stephen returned to Avonlea, Anne helped arrange a reunion at Echo Lodge that resulted in Stephen and Miss Lavendar reconciling. Anne and Diana subsequently helped Miss Lavendar prepare for her wedding, and she married Stephen in her garden before departing, leaving Echo Lodge temporarily closed. Following her marriage, she later hosted Anne for a summer visit, gently questioning her about her disrupted relationship with Gilbert Blythe.

label: Quote
value: Lavendar Lewis said: "But oh, won’t you stay and have tea with me? Please, do. Mr. Kimball’s will have tea over before you get there. And Charlotta the Fourth and I will be so glad to have you."

label: Quote
value: Lavendar Lewis said: "It gave me a shock to hear about Stephen’s son that first day you were here, Anne. I’ve never been able to mention him to you since, but I’ve wanted to know all about him. What sort of a boy is he?"

label: Quote
value: Lavendar Lewis said: "Oh, I’m not so old as I thought . . . and I don’t need a single blue pill! Girls, when you come back with your strawberries we’ll have tea out here under the silver poplar. I’ll have it all ready for you with home-grown cream."

label: Quote
value: Lavendar Lewis said: "About your age I think. He ought to be older because I dreamed him long before you were born. But I’ll never let him get any older than eleven or twelve; because if I did some day he might grow up altogether and then I’d lose him."

label: Quote
value: Lavendar Lewis said: "I’m wholesomely ashamed to think that a new dress . . . even it is a forget-me-not organdy . . . should exhilarate me so, when a good conscience and an extra contribution to Foreign Missions couldn’t do it."

label: History
value: Rachel Lynde was married
unit: Rachel Lynde was married at the age of eighteen. Living in Avonlea, she offered unsolicited advice to Anne Shirley before Anne confronted Miss Josephine Barry over a misunderstanding, and she later visited Green Gables to praise Anne's growth and character at the end of a school term. When Matthew Cuthbert secretly sought her help to buy Anne a modern dress, Lynde sewed a stylish brown dress with puffed sleeves for the girl. As Anne matured, Lynde walked home with her while discussing church preparations, and she was present at Green Gables alongside Marilla and the Keith twins to warmly welcome Anne back for the Christmas holiday during Anne's first term at Redmond College. Her misadventures in Avonlea later became a topic of local news relayed to Anne by Davy Keith while she was away at university.

label: History
value: Marilla Cuthbert was raised in Avonlea.
unit: Marilla Cuthbert was raised in Avonlea, having moved into the new house at Green Gables when she was already grown up. In her youth, she quarreled with John Blythe and refused his request for forgiveness, a decision that led to their permanent estrangement and a lifetime of hidden regrets. When her brother Matthew accidentally brought home an orphan girl named Anne Shirley instead of the boy they had requested, Marilla initially planned to return her, but she ultimately relented after learning of Anne's neglected childhood and agreeing to raise her. Over the following years, Marilla navigated the challenges of raising the imaginative girl, enduring public embarrassments like Anne's explosive outburst at Mrs. Rachel Lynde and accidental disasters such as a liniment-flavored cake. As their bond deepened, Marilla suffered intense panic and realized how deeply she loved Anne after the girl broke her ankle, and she later stood by her when Anne mistakenly dyed her hair green. Following Matthew's sudden death from shock, Marilla learned that her own failing eyesight would prevent her from managing Green Gables alone, but she was saved from selling the farm when Anne gave up her college scholarship to remain at home. After the death of her cousin Mary Keith, Marilla took in two orphaned twins, Davy and Dora, whose rowdy behavior presented fresh household trials. To ensure that Anne could attend Redmond College, Marilla invited the recently widowed Rachel Lynde to move into Green Gables and share the home. Through all of Anne's years away at school and subsequent return home, Marilla remained a steady anchor, managing the household alongside Mrs. Lynde while watching Anne mature into adulthood.

When her brother Matthew accidentally brought home an orphan girl named Anne Shirley instead of the boy they had requested, Marilla initially planned to return her, but she ultimately relented after learning of Anne's neglected childhood and agreeing to raise her. Over the following years, Marilla navigated the challenges of raising the imaginative girl, enduring public embarrassments like Anne's explosive outburst at Mrs. Rachel Lynde and accidental disasters such as a liniment-flavored cake. As their bond deepened, Marilla suffered intense panic and realized how deeply she loved Anne after the girl broke her ankle, and she later stood by her when Anne mistakenly dyed her hair green. Following Matthew's sudden death from shock, Marilla learned that her own failing eyesight would prevent her from managing Green Gables alone, but she was saved from selling the farm when Anne gave up her college scholarship to remain at home. After the death of her cousin Mary Keith, Marilla took in two orphaned twins, Davy and Dora, whose rowdy behavior presented fresh household trials. To ensure that Anne could attend Redmond College, Marilla invited the recently widowed Rachel Lynde to move into Green Gables and share the home. Through all of Anne's years away at school and subsequent return home, Marilla remained a steady anchor, managing the household alongside Mrs. Lynde while watching Anne mature into adulthood.

label: Quote
value: Marilla Cuthbert said: "No, I don’t want any of your imaginings. Just you stick to bald facts. Begin at the beginning. Where were you born and how old are you?"

label: Quote
value: Marilla Cuthbert said: "We’re not talking about poetry, Anne—we are talking about saying your prayers. Don’t you know it’s a terrible wicked thing not to say your prayers every night? I’m afraid you are a very bad little girl."

label: Quote
value: Marilla Cuthbert said: "Well, you’ll have to do without your thrill. I hadn’t any material to waste on puffed sleeves. I think they are ridiculous-looking things anyhow. I prefer the plain, sensible ones."

label: History
value: Matthew Cuthbert was raised by a shy, silent father.
unit: Matthew Cuthbert was raised by a shy, silent father who built a home far away from other people, and Matthew grew up to be the first person to offer love and sympathy to Anne Shirley's starved childhood. When he went to the station expecting to pick up an orphan boy to help on the farm, he was met instead by Anne and decided to bring her to Green Gables to let his sister Marilla handle the mistake. Matthew quietly advocated for keeping Anne and gave her simple delights, such as visiting her room to gently persuade her to apologize to Mrs. Lynde so she could stay, and gifting her a package of chocolate sweets. After Anne completed her studies at Queen's Academy, Matthew spent a tender final evening with her before dying suddenly from the shock of reading about the Abbey Bank failure.

value: Matthew Cuthbert said: “Well now, you’ll have to punish her,” said Matthew, reaching for his hat. “I’ve nothing to do with it, remember. You warned me off yourself.”

value: Matthew Cuthbert said: “Well now, I can’t seem to,” said Matthew, as he opened the yard gate to let the cows through. “It’s only that I’m getting old, Anne, and keep forgetting it. Well, well, I’ve always worked pretty hard and I’d rather drop in harness.”

value: Matthew Cuthbert said: "I reckon she ought to be punished a little. But don’t be too hard on her, Marilla. Recollect she hasn’t ever had anyone to teach her right. You’re—you’re going to give her something to eat, aren’t you?"

unit: Matthew Cuthbert and his sister Marilla lived at Green Gables, having grown up before the new house was built. Having worn a soft brown beard since he was twenty, Matthew drove to the train station to pick up an orphan boy, but instead brought home Anne Shirley. Although Marilla initially intended to return the girl, Matthew persistently desired to keep her, and Marilla ultimately agreed. He consistently supported Anne, encouraging her enthusiasm when Marilla criticized her activities and gently advising her on matters of romance and imagination. On one Christmas, Matthew braved his shyness to buy Anne a stylish brown dress with puffed sleeves after noticing how plain her clothing was compared to her peers. When Anne placed first on the island for the Queen's Academy entrance examinations, she proudly shared the news with Matthew and Marilla. Later, Matthew helped Anne prepare for her departure to Queen's Academy as she pursued her higher education.

value: Matthew said: “There, there, Marilla, you can have your own way,” said Matthew reassuringly. “Only be as good and kind to her as you can without spoiling her. I kind of think she’s one of the sort you can do anything with if you only get her to love you.”

label: Quote
value: Matthew said: “Well now, I guess you’ll manage all right,” said Matthew, looking at Anne’s white little face and the dark shadows under her eyes. “You just go right to bed and have a good sleep. I’ll do all the chores.”

label: Quote
value: Matthew said: “Well now, I’m much obliged,” said Matthew, “and—and—I dunno—but I’d like—I think they make the sleeves different nowadays to what they used to be. If it wouldn’t be asking too much I—I’d like them made in the new way.”

label: Quote
value: Matthew said: "We must see what we can do for her some of these days, Marilla. I guess she’ll need something more than Avonlea school by and by."

label: Quote
value: Matthew said: "Well now, I ain’t interfering. It ain’t interfering to have your own opinion. And my opinion is that you ought to let Anne go."

However, as Paul grows older during a summer in Avonlea, he begins to lose these imaginative shoreline visions.

label: Quote
value: Paul Irving said: "I’ve eaten enough to make anyone grow. I do hope, now that I’ve begun, I’ll keep on till I’m as tall as father. He is six feet, you know, Miss Lavendar."

label: Quote
value: Paul Irving said: "I think you would make a splendid mother. You have just the right look in your eyes . . . the look my little mother always had. I think it’s a pity you haven’t any boys of your own."

label: Quote
value: Paul Irving said: "you can’t think what has happened! Something so splendid. Father is here . . . just think of that! Father is here! Come right in. Father, this is my beautiful teacher. You know, father."

label: Quote
value: Paul Irving said: "and I came back to give them to you because I thought you were the kind of lady that would like them, and because . . ."

label: Quote
value: Paul Irving said: “Yes; but if dryads are foolish they must take the consequences, just as if they were real people,” said Paul gravely. “Do you know what I think about the new moon, teacher? I think it is a little golden boat full of dreams.”

label: History
value: Philippa Gordon is the daughter of a wealthy man from an old Nova Scotia family.
unit: Philippa "Phil" Gordon, the daughter of a wealthy man from an old Nova Scotia family, met Anne Shirley and Priscilla Grant during her first day at Redmond College, where they quickly bonded over shared homesickness. Phil became a central member of the friend group, joining Anne and Priscilla in renting Patty's Place alongside Stella Maynard and Aunt Jamesina. Though initially courted by numerous suitors back home and pursued by men at college, Phil's life took a major turn during a summer at Prospect Point. There, she met Jonas Blake, a theological student whose moving sermon earned her deep admiration. Phil accepted Jonas's marriage proposal later that school year, choosing him over her wealthy suitors. Throughout their time at Redmond, Phil served as a close confidante to Anne, comforting her through her complicated romantic trials, including her rejection of Roy Gardner. After completing her time at college, Phil celebrated her wedding with her friends in attendance.

unit: Philippa "Phil" Gordon, the daughter of a wealthy man from an old Nova Scotia family, met Anne Shirley and Priscilla Grant during her first day at Redmond College, where they quickly bonded over shared homesickness. Phil became a central member of the friend group, joining Anne and Priscilla in renting Patty's Place alongside Stella Maynard and Aunt Jamesina. Though initially courted by numerous suitors back home and pursued by men at college, Phil's life took a major turn during a summer at Prospect Point. There, she met Jonas Blake, a theological student whose moving sermon earned her deep admiration. Phil accepted Jonas's marriage proposal later that school year, choosing him over her wealthy suitors. Throughout their time at Redmond, Phil served as a close confidante to Anne, comforting her through her complicated romantic trials, including her rejection of Roy Gardner. After completing her time at college, Phil celebrated her wedding with her friends in attendance.

label: Quote
value: Phil Gordon said: "Heaps. The boys like me awfully—they really do. But there were only two that mattered. The rest were all too young and too poor. I must marry a rich man, you know."

label: Quote
value: Phil Gordon said: "And let me come to see you. I want to be chummy with you. I’ve taken such a fancy to you both. And I haven’t quite disgusted you with my frivolity, have I?"

label: Quote
value: Phil Gordon said: "I’ll go, if I can walk with Priscilla and Charlie. That will be a bearable degree of gooseberry. That Gilbert of yours is a darling, Anne, but why does he go around so much with Goggle-eyes?"

label: Quote
value: Phil Gordon said: "I don’t want William’s Island especially, but I’m sure I couldn’t get it if I did. Look at that sentry on the summit of the fort, right beside the flag. Doesn’t he look as if he had stepped out of a romance?"

label: Quote
value: Phil Gordon said: "Look—in white letters, around the archway over the gate. ‘Patty’s Place.’ Isn’t that killing? Especially on this Avenue of Pinehursts and Elmwolds and Cedarcrofts? ‘Patty’s Place,’ if you please! I adore it."

unit: Priscilla Grant attended Queen's Academy alongside Anne Shirley, and she later worked as a teacher at Carmody school. During a spring birthday outing, she explored the woods and Hester Gray's forgotten garden with Anne, Diana, and Jane. She eventually wrote to Anne to explain why famous author Mrs. Morgan had missed a planned dinner party, but she later accompanied Mrs. Morgan to Green Gables herself, arriving while Anne was dealing with a dyed nose. When Anne moved to Kingsport to begin her studies at Redmond College, Priscilla met her at the train station and brought her to their initial boardinghouse. Soon after, while visiting a cemetery, Priscilla and Anne befriended Philippa Gordon, quickly expanding their social circle at college. Looking to improve their living situation for their second year, Priscilla joined Anne in arranging to rent a house called Patty's Place alongside Stella Maynard and Philippa. She continued to share in the domestic and social life at Patty's Place throughout her remaining time at Redmond, visiting Anne in Avonlea over the summer and ultimately completing her studies to graduate alongside her friends on Convocation day.

label: History
value: Mrs. Rachel Lynde lived as Marilla Cuthbert's neighbor for forty-five years.
unit: Mrs. Rachel Lynde, a longtime Avonlea resident who raised ten children, buried two, and knitted sixteen cotton warp quilts, lived as Marilla Cuthbert's neighbor for forty-five years. She initially expressed strong disapproval when Matthew and Marilla decided to adopt an orphan, and she later engaged in a fierce argument with young Anne Shirley after insulting the girl's appearance, though she quickly accepted Anne's dramatic apology. Mrs. Lynde frequently offered advice on community affairs, cautioning Anne against forming a Village Improvement Society and later confirming that Anne had earned her students' respect after a necessary spanking at school. She actively tracked local events, investigating the unexpected arrival of Mr. Harrison's long-lost wife and keeping up with neighborhood news. Following the death of her husband, Thomas, Marilla proposed that Mrs. Lynde move into Green Gables so Anne could leave her teaching position to attend Redmond College. Residing at Green Gables alongside Marilla and the orphaned twins, Davy and Dora, Mrs. Lynde maintained her role as a central source of local gossip. She kept Anne informed about community developments during her college breaks, including news of Ruby Gillis's terminal illness and Diana Barry's upcoming marriage.

label: Quote

label: History
value: Royal Gardner was a handsome Redmond student.
unit: Royal Gardner was a handsome Redmond student who had previously left college and gone abroad for two years due to his mother's failing health. He met Anne Shirley during a sudden rainstorm, rescuing her with his umbrella and walking her home before sending her a dozen roses. After escorting Anne to a reception and introducing his mother and sisters to her, Roy took her to the harbor pavilion upon their college graduation and proposed. However, Anne realized she did not love him and refused his offer, leaving Roy deeply upset as they parted ways.

unit: Royal Gardner was a handsome Redmond student who had previously left college and gone abroad for two years due to his mother's failing health. He met Anne Shirley during a sudden rainstorm, rescuing her with his umbrella and walking her home before sending her a dozen roses. After escorting Anne to a reception and introducing his mother and sisters to her, Roy took her to the harbor pavilion upon their college graduation and proposed. However, Anne realized she did not love him and refused his offer, leaving Roy deeply upset as they parted ways.

label: Quote
value: Roy Gardner said: "That ought to be sufficient introduction. My name is Royal Gardner. And you are the Miss Shirley who read the Tennyson paper at the Philomathic the other evening, aren’t you?"

label: Quote
value: Roy Gardner said: "I feel as if I didn’t belong anywhere yet. I put in my Freshman and Sophomore years at Redmond two years ago. I’ve been in Europe ever since. Now I’ve come back to finish my Arts course."

label: Quote
value: Roy Gardner said: "I can’t understand it—I can’t believe you are not the woman I’ve believed you to be. But reproaches are idle between us. You are the only woman I can ever love. I thank you for your friendship, at least. Good-bye, Anne."

label: Quote
value: Roy Gardner said: "So we are classmates as well as collegemates. I am reconciled to the loss of the years that the locust has eaten,"

label: Quote
value: Roy Gardner said: "Pardon me—may I offer you the shelter of my umbrella?"

label: Appearance
value: Ruby Gillis is a fair young woman.
unit: Ruby Gillis is a fair young woman known for her long yellow, golden braids of hair, large bright-blue eyes, and a brilliant complexion. Originally characterized by a plump and showy figure with snap and color, her appearance later changes as she becomes very thin. In addition, her blue eyes take on a bright, lustrous sheen, and her cheeks display a hectically brilliant color.

label: Personality
value: Ruby Gillis is cheerful.
unit: Ruby Gillis is a cheerful, good-tempered individual who enjoys life's pleasantries, though she is prone to hysterics and harbors a mortal dread of fat green caterpillars. Driven by a desire for romance, her long-held ambition is to have a multitude of suitors fascinated by her, planning to teach for only two years before marrying and settling down after having a gay time. She is noted for being highly conscious of young men, rarely speaking of anything other than boys and the compliments they give her. Later in life, however, she expresses a profound fear of dying.

label: History
value: Ruby Gillis grew up alongside Anne Shirley
unit: Ruby Gillis grew up alongside Anne Shirley, having charmed away all her warts as a young girl using a magic pebble given to her by old Mary Joe from the Creek. As a child, she openly expressed her intention to have dozens of beaus when she grew up, and she eventually joined Anne's local story club to cultivate her imagination. She later attended school and Queen's Academy in the same class as Anne. By her early twenties, Ruby became well known in Avonlea for her lively social life and frequent flirtations. However, she eventually contracted consumption, a terminal illness that brought about a rapid decline in her health despite her efforts to maintain a cheerful, flirtatious façade. During a visit from Anne, Ruby broke down in her garden and tearfully confessed her deep fear of dying and her yearning to go on living. Shortly after Anne left her that evening, Ruby passed away peacefully in her sleep, and her friends later gathered for her funeral.

unit: Ruby Gillis grew up alongside Anne Shirley, having charmed away all her warts as a young girl using a magic pebble given to her by old Mary Joe from the Creek. As a child, she openly expressed her intention to have dozens of beaus when she grew up, and she eventually joined Anne's local story club to cultivate her imagination. She later attended school and Queen's Academy in the same class as Anne. By her early twenties, Ruby became well known in Avonlea for her lively social life and frequent flirtations. However, she eventually contracted consumption, a terminal illness that brought about a rapid decline in her health despite her efforts to maintain a cheerful, flirtatious façade. During a visit from Anne, Ruby broke down in her garden and tearfully confessed her deep fear of dying and her yearning to go on living. Shortly after Anne left her that evening, Ruby passed away peacefully in her sleep, and her friends later gathered for her funeral.

label: Quote
value: Ruby Gillis said: "I don’t mind floating down when there’s two or three of us in the flat and we can sit up. It’s fun then. But to lie down and pretend I was dead—I just couldn’t. I’d die really of fright."

label: Quote
value: Ruby Gillis said: "It makes me feel frightened, girls. Do you suppose it’s really right to act like this? Mrs. Lynde says that all play-acting is abominably wicked."

label: Quote
value: Ruby Gillis said: "Anne, it won’t be long now before I’ll be lying over there. You and Diana and all the rest will be going about, full of life—and I’ll be there—in the old graveyard—dead!"

label: Quote
value: Ruby Gillis said: "I’ll try. I’ll think over what you have said, and try to believe it. And you’ll come up as often as you can, won’t you, Anne?"

label: Quote
value: Ruby Gillis said: "There’s a concert at Carmody and a party at White Sands. Herb Spencer’s going to take me. He’s my latest. Be sure to come up tomorrow. I’m dying for a good talk with you. I want to hear all about your doings at Redmond."

label: History
value: Rusty was found thin.
unit: After being found thin, singed, and damaged, Rusty trotted close to Anne's heels as he followed her home, having recently fought and defeated the tobacco-king's cat. Anne reluctantly adopted the disreputable stray at Patty's Place, where he miraculously survived a chloroforming attempt and earned a permanent spot in the house. Upon Aunt Jamesina's arrival with her own pets, Rusty attempted to fight the newcomers, getting put in his place by the Sarah-cat while engaging in repeated battles with Joseph before eventually becoming his close friend. He later contributed to a chaotic scene at Patty's Place when Royal Gardner's mother and sisters made an unexpected visit.

label: History
value: Miss Sarah Copp lived at the Copp home on the Tory Road.
unit: Miss Sarah Copp lived at the Copp home on the Tory Road, where she had been forced by her sister Martha to whitewash an old duck house every spring. After Anne Shirley fell through the roof of the duck house while trying to look into the pantry, Sarah rescued her and later entertained Anne and Diana Wright over tea and bread, selling Anne a willow-ware platter and announcing her own upcoming marriage. Her father had previously sent away her suitor, Luther Wallace, twenty years earlier because he was poor. In addition, Aunt Jamesina possessed a pet named the Sarah-cat, who had been given to her by her washerwoman and who quickly put the stray cat Rusty in his place upon arriving at Patty's Place.

label: History
value: Stacy served as the schoolteacher in Avonlea.
unit: Miss Stacy served as the schoolteacher in Avonlea, maintaining order without ever whipping her pupils. Upon starting her tenure, she proposed organizing a Christmas concert to raise funds for a school flag, which her students eagerly embraced. At the end of her first term, she announced she would return the following year to prepare students for the Queen's Entrance examination, subsequently guiding them through their studies for the crucial tests. She eventually left Avonlea after accepting a position at a grade school in her home district.

label: Quote
value: Stella Maynard said: "I love Anne and I like Roy. Everybody says she is making a brilliant match, and even Mrs. Gardner thinks her charming now. It all sounds as if it were made in heaven, but I have my doubts. Make the most of that, Aunt Jamesina."

label: Quote
value: Stella Maynard said: "I was afraid they’d come back. And then our jolly little nest here would be broken up—and we poor callow nestlings thrown out on the cruel world of boardinghouses again."

label: Quote
value: Stella Maynard said: "Nothing seems worthwhile. My very thoughts are old. I’ve thought them all before. What is the use of living after all, Anne?"

label: Quote
value: Stella Maynard said: "Oh, my mind agrees with you, Anne. But my soul remains doleful and uninspired. I’m always grubby and dingy on rainy nights."

label: Quote
value: Stella Maynard said: "Philippa Gordon! I never thought you were utterly unfeeling. The idea of you saying you’d love to break a man’s heart!"

label: History
value: Walter is the father of Anne.
unit: Walter was the father of Anne, who died of fever alongside his wife, Bertha, when Anne was only three months old. His death left Anne an orphan, forcing her into a childhood of moving between families and caring for children before being sent to an asylum. Years later, Anne visited Walter's former home in Bolingbroke and his grave, where she received and read a packet of old love letters written between Walter and Bertha, finally allowing her to feel deeply connected to her parents.

value: Marilla returns to Green Gables.
chapter: v2 · VIII Marilla Adopts Twins
unit: Marilla returns to Green Gables with the orphaned twins, Davy and Dora, whose playful and rowdy behavior immediately poses a challenge for Marilla and Anne. At church on Sunday, Davy creates a commotion by dropping a caterpillar down Lauretta White's neck during the service. Later in the week, Davy ruins Dora's dress by forcing her to walk the pigpen fence and pumps water over her, subsequently confessing to Anne that he also hid a toad in Marilla's bed.

chapter: v2 · V A Full-fledged Schoolma’am
unit: Anne begins her first day teaching school, forgetting her prepared speech but managing her new pupils, including the sullen Anthony Pye and a bright, imaginative boy named Paul Irving. After school, an excessively dressed Mrs. Donnell visits to demand specific pronunciations and names for her children. On her walk home, Paul gives Anne wild orchids, brightening her mood before she returns to recount her day to Marilla Cuthbert and Rachel Lynde.

value: Anne bids a tearful farewell to her home at Green Gables.
chapter: v3 · Chapter III Greeting and Farewell
unit: Anne bids a tearful farewell to her home at Green Gables and leaves for Redmond College with Gilbert and Charlie Sloane. After a rainy drive to the station and a boat ride from Charlottetown, she and Gilbert travel by train to Kingsport. Upon arrival, Anne is warmly met by Priscilla Grant, who takes her by cab to their new boardinghouse while cheering her up.

value: Philippa Gordon chats exuberantly with Anne.

unit: Philippa Gordon chats exuberantly with Anne and Priscilla about her suitors back home, her reluctance to grow up, and her impressions of Redmond College. label: v3 · Chapter VI In the Park
value: Anne goes for an afternoon walk.
chapter: v3 · Chapter VI In the Park
unit: Anne, Priscilla, and Phil Gordon go for an afternoon walk with Gilbert and Charlie Sloane through the park and along the harbor shore. After watching the sunset from a pavilion, they walk back via Spofford Avenue where Phil points out a charming, quaint house called Patty's Place. Anne feels an instant connection to the house and has a strong presentiment that she will become better acquainted with it.

label: v3 · Chapter VII Home Again
value: Anne finishes term examinations at Redmond College.
chapter: v3 · Chapter VII Home Again
unit: After finishing term examinations at Redmond College, Anne returns home to Green Gables for the Christmas holiday where she is warmly greeted by Diana, Marilla, Mrs. Lynde, and the twins. That night, Anne helps a troubled Davy through a dilemma about wanting to say a bad word so that he feels ready to say his prayers. During the break, Anne receives letters from her friends, shares news with her family, and visits Echo Lodge with Diana to air out the house and listen to the echoes once more.

label: v3 · Chapter VII Home Again
value: Anne finishes term examinations at Redmond College.
chapter: v3 · Chapter VII Home Again
unit: After finishing term examinations at Redmond College, Anne returns home to Green Gables for the Christmas holiday where she is warmly greeted by Diana, Marilla, Mrs. Lynde, and the twins. That night, Anne helps a troubled Davy through a dilemma about wanting to say a bad word so that he feels ready to say his prayers. During the break, Anne receives letters from her friends, shares news with her family, and visits Echo Lodge with Diana to air out the house and listen to the echoes once more.

unit: Suffering from a severe toothache, Anne has a disastrous and irritable day at school, accidentally throwing a package of fireworks into the stove and later whipping Anthony Pye for putting a mouse in her desk. She returns home distraught over losing her temper, but Marilla comforts her. The next day, to Anne's surprise, Anthony shows newfound respect for her, which Mrs. Rachel Lynde later confirms was earned through the whipping.

unit: Anne joins Marilla, Mrs. Rachel, Dora, and Davy outside on a June evening. Davy complains about his schoolwork and the local funerals, but Anne offers to help him with his arithmetic. Anne later wanders down to Dryad's Bubble, feeling melancholic about Gilbert's absence and the changes that growing up brings.

unit: Marilla returns to Green Gables with the orphaned twins, Davy and Dora, whose playful and rowdy behavior immediately poses a challenge for Marilla and Anne. Later in the week, Davy ruins Dora's dress by forcing her to walk the pigpen fence and pumps water over her, subsequently confessing to Anne that he also hid a toad in Marilla's bed.

unit: Anne converses with Mr. Harrison on his porch about Rachel Lynde, Davy's antics, and the Village Improvement Society's hall painting project. The Improvers gather at Green Gables in despair over the blunder, but the town's sympathy ultimately turns in their favor against the Pyes.

label: v2 · XVIII An Adventure on the Tory Road
value: Davy questions Anne about sleep.
chapter: v2 · XVIII An Adventure on the Tory Road
unit: Davy questions Anne about sleep and Marilla's frugality before Marilla calls Anne over to see Diana's signal. Diana tells Anne about a willow-ware platter at the Copp home on the Tory Road, which they decide to retrieve the following day. When they arrive at the empty Copp house, Anne climbs onto an old duck house to look through the pantry window, falls through the roof, and gets trapped. After sitting through a rainstorm while stuck, Anne is rescued by Miss Sarah Copp, who agrees to entertain selling her the platter over tea.

When they arrive at the empty Copp house, Anne climbs onto an old duck house to look through the pantry window, falls through the roof, and gets trapped. After sitting through a rainstorm while stuck, Anne is rescued by Miss Sarah Copp, who agrees to entertain selling her the platter over tea.

chapter: v2 · XIX Just a Happy Day
unit: Anne visits Paul Irving for tea, reassuring him about his imaginative thoughts and helping him feel better after a maid called him strange. chapter: v2 · XXIV A Prophet in His Own Country
unit: After anonymous newspaper notes predict a severe storm, an unusually devastating hailstorm strikes Avonlea, severely damaging crops, trees, and windows. At Green Gables, Anne, Marilla, and the twins shelter through the tempest, later learning that Mr. Harrison's parrot was killed and an eyesore house was struck by lightning. Neighbors assess the ruin, and Uncle Abe basks in his newly acquired fame as a prophet.

Anne later wanders down to Dryad's Bubble, feeling melancholic about Gilbert's absence and the changes that growing up brings.

label: v2 · II Selling in Haste and Repenting at Leisure
value: Anne and Diana spot a Jersey cow in Mr. Harrison's wet oat field while driving back from Carmody.
chapter: v2 · II Selling in Haste and Repenting at Leisure
unit: While driving back from Carmody, Anne and Diana spot a Jersey cow in Mr. Harrison's wet oat field and chase it into the lane. Believing the cow to be her own mischievous animal, Dolly, an annoyed Anne impetuously sells it on the spot to Mr. Shearer for twenty dollars. Upon returning home to Green Gables, Anne discovers her real cow still in the milking pen and realizes she accidentally sold Mr. Harrison's cow. However, chaos ensues when Davy ruins the lemon pies, the peas are ruined by being oversweetened by too many cooks, and Mrs. Morgan fails to show up. To cap off the disastrous day, Miss Barry's expensive platter is accidentally smashed, and Anne later receives a letter explaining Mrs. Morgan injured her ankle.

label: v2 · XVIII An Adventure on the Tory Road
value: Davy questions Anne about sleep.
chapter: v2 · XVIII An Adventure on the Tory Road
unit: Davy questions Anne about sleep and Marilla's frugality before Marilla calls Anne over to see Diana's signal. Diana tells Anne about a willow-ware platter at the Copp home on the Tory Road, which they decide to retrieve the following day. When they arrive at the empty Copp house, Anne climbs onto an old duck house to look through the pantry window, falls through the roof, and gets trapped. After sitting through a rainstorm while stuck, Anne is rescued by Miss Sarah Copp, who agrees to entertain selling her the platter over tea.

unit: Anne converses with Mr. Harrison on his porch about Rachel Lynde, Davy's antics, and the Village Improvement Society's hall painting project. The Improvers gather at Green Gables in despair over the blunder, but the town's sympathy ultimately turns in their favor against the Pyes.

label: v2 · XXIV A Prophet in His Own Country
value: Anonymous newspaper notes predict a severe storm.
chapter: v2 · XXIV A Prophet in His Own Country
unit: After anonymous newspaper notes predict a severe storm, an unusually devastating hailstorm strikes Avonlea, severely damaging crops, trees, and windows. At Green Gables, Anne, Marilla, and the twins shelter through the tempest, later learning that Mr. Harrison's parrot was killed and an eyesore house was struck by lightning. Neighbors assess the ruin, and Uncle Abe basks in his newly acquired fame as a prophet.

label: v3 · Chapter VII Home Again

chapter: v3 · Chapter VII Home Again
unit: After finishing term examinations at Redmond College, Anne returns home to Green Gables for the Christmas holiday where she is warmly greeted by Diana, Marilla, Mrs. Lynde, and the twins. That night, Anne helps a troubled Davy through a dilemma about wanting to say a bad word so that he feels ready to say his prayers. During the break, Anne receives letters from her friends, shares news with her family, and visits Echo Lodge with Diana to air out the house and listen to the echoes once more.

value: Matthew convinces Marilla to let Anne attend a Debating Club concert.
chapter: v1 · CHAPTER XIX. A Concert, a Catastrophe, and a Confession
unit: After Matthew convinces Marilla to let Anne attend a Debating Club concert and spend the night at Diana's, Anne and Diana enjoy the event together. Upon returning home, they leap into the spare-room bed as a game, unwittingly jumping directly onto Diana's visiting great-aunt, Aunt Josephine. The resulting uproar leaves Miss Barry furious and threatens Diana's music lessons, prompting a remorseful Anne to seek a way to make amends.

value: Anonymous newspaper notes predict a severe storm.
chapter: v2 · XXIV A Prophet in His Own Country
unit: After anonymous newspaper notes predict a severe storm, an unusually devastating hailstorm strikes Avonlea, severely damaging crops, trees, and windows. At Green Gables, Anne, Marilla, and the twins shelter through the tempest, later learning that Mr. Harrison's parrot was killed and an eyesore house was struck by lightning. Neighbors assess the ruin, and Uncle Abe basks in his newly acquired fame as a prophet.

unit: Anne and Diana visit Echo Lodge to help Charlotta the Fourth and Miss Lavendar prepare for the upcoming wedding. The next day, Miss Lavendar and Stephen Irving are married in the garden in front of their guests, after which everyone sees them off at the station. While locking up the stone house afterward, Anne and Gilbert share a quiet, poignant moment that subtly alters the nature of their relationship as they look toward their college years.

unit: Anne, Priscilla, and Phil Gordon go for an afternoon walk with Gilbert and Charlie Sloane through the park and along the harbor shore. After watching the sunset from a pavilion, they walk back via Spofford Avenue where Phil points out a charming, quaint house called Patty's Place. Anne feels an instant connection to the house and has a strong presentiment that she will become better acquainted with it.

label: v3 · Chapter VII Home Again
value: Anne finishes term examinations at Redmond College.
chapter: v3 · Chapter VII Home Again
unit: After finishing term examinations at Redmond College, Anne returns home to Green Gables for the Christmas holiday where she is warmly greeted by Diana, Marilla, Mrs. Lynde, and the twins. That night, Anne helps a troubled Davy through a dilemma about wanting to say a bad word so that he feels ready to say his prayers. During the break, Anne receives letters from her friends, shares news with her family, and visits Echo Lodge with Diana to air out the house and listen to the echoes once more.

value: Anne and Diana spot a Jersey cow in Mr. Harrison's wet oat field while driving back from Carmody.
chapter: v2 · II Selling in Haste and Repenting at Leisure
unit: While driving back from Carmody, Anne and Diana spot a Jersey cow in Mr. Harrison's wet oat field and chase it into the lane. Believing the cow to be her own mischievous animal, Dolly, an annoyed Anne impetuously sells it on the spot to Mr. Shearer for twenty dollars. Upon returning home to Green Gables, Anne discovers her real cow still in the milking pen and realizes she accidentally sold Mr. Harrison's cow. Horrified by her mistake, Anne packs a freshly baked nut cake as a peace offering and sets off to confess to Mr. Harrison.

unit: Anne converses with Mr. Harrison on his porch about Rachel Lynde, Davy's antics, and the Village Improvement Society's hall painting project. The Improvers gather at Green Gables in despair over the blunder, but the town's sympathy ultimately turns in their favor against the Pyes.

unit: Suffering from a severe toothache, Anne has a disastrous and irritable day at school, accidentally throwing a package of fireworks into the stove and later whipping Anthony Pye for putting a mouse in her desk. chapter: v2 · XXIV A Prophet in His Own Country
unit: After anonymous newspaper notes predict a severe storm, an unusually devastating hailstorm strikes Avonlea, severely damaging crops, trees, and windows. At Green Gables, Anne, Marilla, and the twins shelter through the tempest, later learning that Mr. Harrison's parrot was killed and an eyesore house was struck by lightning. Neighbors assess the ruin, and Uncle Abe basks in his newly acquired fame as a prophet.

value: Anne and Diana visit Echo Lodge
chapter: v2 · XXX A Wedding at the Stone House
unit: Anne and Diana visit Echo Lodge to help Charlotta the Fourth and Miss Lavendar prepare for the upcoming wedding. The next day, Miss Lavendar and Stephen Irving are married in the garden in front of their guests, after which everyone sees them off at the station. While locking up the stone house afterward, Anne and Gilbert share a quiet, poignant moment that subtly alters the nature of their relationship as they look toward their college years.

unit: Anne returns to Avonlea for a snowbound and lonely Christmas vacation, feeling embarrassed by Gilbert's romantic attentions and worried about her finances for her next year at Redmond. However, a letter arrives revealing that Miss Josephine Barry has died and left Anne a thousand dollars in her will, securing her financial future.

unit: While Marilla and Mrs. Lynde attend a political rally in Charlottetown, Anne and Matthew spend a quiet evening together studying and talking. Diana Barry rushes in to beg for help because her sister Minnie May is gravely ill with croup while their parents are away. Anne hurries to the Barry home and successfully treats Minnie May using her past experience with Mrs. Hammond's children, saving the baby's life. Touched by Anne's rescue, Mrs. Barry forgives her for the past incident with Diana, allowing the two girls to be best friends once again.

label: v2 · II Selling in Haste and Repenting at Leisure
value: Anne and Diana spot a Jersey cow in Mr. Harrison's wet oat field while driving back from Carmody.
chapter: v2 · II Selling in Haste and Repenting at Leisure
unit: While driving back from Carmody, Anne and Diana spot a Jersey cow in Mr. Harrison's wet oat field and chase it into the lane. Believing the cow to be her own mischievous animal, Dolly, an annoyed Anne impetuously sells it on the spot to Mr. Shearer for twenty dollars. Upon returning home to Green Gables, Anne discovers her real cow still in the milking pen and realizes she accidentally sold Mr. Harrison's cow. Horrified by her mistake, Anne packs a freshly baked nut cake as a peace offering and sets off to confess to Mr. Harrison.

unit: Anne converses with Mr. Harrison on his porch about Rachel Lynde, Davy's antics, and the Village Improvement Society's hall painting project. The Improvers gather at Green Gables in despair over the blunder, but the town's sympathy ultimately turns in their favor against the Pyes.

unit: Suffering from a severe toothache, Anne has a disastrous and irritable day at school, accidentally throwing a package of fireworks into the stove and later whipping Anthony Pye for putting a mouse in her desk. She returns home distraught over losing her temper, but Marilla comforts her. The next day, to Anne's surprise, Anthony shows newfound respect for her, which Mrs. Rachel Lynde later confirms was earned through the whipping.

label: v2 · XVIII An Adventure on the Tory Road
value: Davy questions Anne about sleep.
chapter: v2 · XVIII An Adventure on the Tory Road
unit: Davy questions Anne about sleep and Marilla's frugality before Marilla calls Anne over to see Diana's signal. Diana tells Anne about a willow-ware platter at the Copp home on the Tory Road, which they decide to retrieve the following day. When they arrive at the empty Copp house, Anne climbs onto an old duck house to look through the pantry window, falls through the roof, and gets trapped. After sitting through a rainstorm while stuck, Anne is rescued by Miss Sarah Copp, who agrees to entertain selling her the platter over tea.

unit: After anonymous newspaper notes predict a severe storm, an unusually devastating hailstorm strikes Avonlea, severely damaging crops, trees, and windows. At Green Gables, Anne, Marilla, and the twins shelter through the tempest, later learning that Mr. Harrison's parrot was killed and an eyesore house was struck by lightning. Neighbors assess the ruin, and Uncle Abe basks in his newly acquired fame as a prophet.

unit: After finishing term examinations at Redmond College, Anne returns home to Green Gables for the Christmas holiday where she is warmly greeted by Diana, Marilla, Mrs. Lynde, and the twins. That night, Anne helps a troubled Davy through a dilemma about wanting to say a bad word so that he feels ready to say his prayers. During the break, Anne receives letters from her friends, shares news with her family, and visits Echo Lodge with Diana to air out the house and listen to the echoes once more.

Diana Barry rushes in to beg for help because her sister Minnie May is gravely ill with croup while their parents are away. Anne hurries to the Barry home and successfully treats Minnie May using her past experience with Mrs. Hammond's children, saving the baby's life. Touched by Anne's rescue, Mrs. Barry forgives her for the past incident with Diana, allowing the two girls to be best friends once again.

chapter: v1 · CHAPTER XIX. A Concert, a Catastrophe, and a Confession
unit: After Matthew convinces Marilla to let Anne attend a Debating Club concert and spend the night at Diana's, Anne and Diana enjoy the event together. Upon returning home, they leap into the spare-room bed as a game, unwittingly jumping directly onto Diana's visiting great-aunt, Aunt Josephine. The resulting uproar leaves Miss Barry furious and threatens Diana's music lessons, prompting a remorseful Anne to seek a way to make amends.

chapter: v1 · CHAPTER XIX. A Concert, a Catastrophe, and a Confession
unit: After Matthew convinces Marilla to let Anne attend a Debating Club concert and spend the night at Diana's, Anne and Diana enjoy the event together. Upon returning home, they leap into the spare-room bed as a game, unwittingly jumping directly onto Diana's visiting great-aunt, Aunt Josephine. The resulting uproar leaves Miss Barry furious and threatens Diana's music lessons, prompting a remorseful Anne to seek a way to make amends.

unit: Marilla returns to Green Gables with the orphaned twins, Davy and Dora, whose playful and rowdy behavior immediately poses a challenge for Marilla and Anne. At church on Sunday, Davy creates a commotion by dropping a caterpillar down Lauretta White's neck during the service. Later in the week, Davy ruins Dora's dress by forcing her to walk the pigpen fence and pumps water over her, subsequently confessing to Anne that he also hid a toad in Marilla's bed.

unit: Suffering from a severe toothache, Anne has a disastrous and irritable day at school, accidentally throwing a package of fireworks into the stove and later whipping Anthony Pye for putting a mouse in her desk. The next day, to Anne's surprise, Anthony shows newfound respect for her, which Mrs. Rachel Lynde later confirms was earned through the whipping.

unit: After finishing term examinations at Redmond College, Anne returns home to Green Gables for the Christmas holiday where she is warmly greeted by Diana, Marilla, Mrs. Lynde, and the twins. chapter: v1 · CHAPTER XVIII. Anne to the Rescue
unit: While Marilla and Mrs. Lynde attend a political rally in Charlottetown, Anne and Matthew spend a quiet evening together studying and talking. Diana Barry rushes in to beg for help because her sister Minnie May is gravely ill with croup while their parents are away. Anne hurries to the Barry home and successfully treats Minnie May using her past experience with Mrs. Hammond's children, saving the baby's life. Touched by Anne's rescue, Mrs. Barry forgives her for the past incident with Diana, allowing the two girls to be best friends once again.

Later in the week, Davy ruins Dora's dress by forcing her to walk the pigpen fence and pumps water over her, subsequently confessing to Anne that he also hid a toad in Marilla's bed.

chapter: v2 · IX A Question of Color
unit: Anne converses with Mr. Harrison on his porch about Rachel Lynde, Davy's antics, and the Village Improvement Society's hall painting project. Later, Mrs. Lynde discovers that Joshua Pye has accidentally painted the hall a bright blue instead of green due to a mix-up in color codes. The Improvers gather at Green Gables in despair over the blunder, but the town's sympathy ultimately turns in their favor against the Pyes.

label: v2 · XII A Jonah Day
value: Anne suffers from a severe toothache.
chapter: v2 · XII A Jonah Day
unit: Suffering from a severe toothache, Anne has a disastrous and irritable day at school, accidentally throwing a package of fireworks into the stove and later whipping Anthony Pye for putting a mouse in her desk. She returns home distraught over losing her temper, but Marilla comforts her. The next day, to Anne's surprise, Anthony shows newfound respect for her, which Mrs. Rachel Lynde later confirms was earned through the whipping.

unit: Anne joins Marilla, Mrs. Rachel, Dora, and Davy outside on a June evening. Davy complains about his schoolwork and the local funerals, but Anne offers to help him with his arithmetic. Diana Barry rushes in to beg for help because her sister Minnie May is gravely ill with croup while their parents are away. Anne hurries to the Barry home and successfully treats Minnie May using her past experience with Mrs. Hammond's children, saving the baby's life. Touched by Anne's rescue, Mrs. Barry forgives her for the past incident with Diana, allowing the two girls to be best friends once again.

As the school year progresses, Anne matures into a quieter fifteen-year-old girl, growing taller than Marilla and shifting her focus to simple, disciplined writing. Marilla feels a sense of loss over Anne growing up, while Anne worries about the anxiety and potential failure surrounding the crucial exams.

chapter: v1 · CHAPTER XXXII. The Pass List Is Out
unit: Anne completes her school term and travels to Charlottetown for the Queen's Academy entrance examinations. After weeks of anxious waiting, Diana rushes to Green Gables with the published results to reveal that Anne has tied for first place on the Island alongside Gilbert Blythe. Overjoyed, Anne shares the proud news with Matthew, Marilla, and Mrs. Lynde before ending her night with a thankful prayer.

unit: Anne and Diana excitedly prepare a elaborate dinner and floral decorations at Green Gables for a guest, Mrs. Morgan. However, chaos ensues when Davy ruins the lemon pies, the peas are ruined by being oversweetened by too many cooks, and Mrs. Morgan fails to show up. To cap off the disastrous day, Miss Barry's expensive platter is accidentally smashed, and Anne later receives a letter explaining Mrs. Morgan injured her ankle.

Mr. Barry carries Anne home, where Marilla experiences a deep realization of how much she cares for the girl. Bedridden for seven weeks while her ankle heals, Anne receives many visitors and eagerly anticipates returning to school to meet her new teacher, Miss Stacy.

chapter: v1 · CHAPTER XXX. The Queen’s Class Is Organized
unit: Marilla informs Anne that Miss Stacy visited to recommend that she join an advanced class preparing for the Queen's Entrance examination. Anne is thrilled at the opportunity to study toward becoming a teacher and gladly accepts. After the class is organized, Anne navigates the dynamic of studying alongside her peers—including her rival, Gilbert Blythe—while missing Diana, who is not taking the exam.
